title: Canonicalize all root paths before comparison to eliminate case/8.3 spelling bugs
context: Root comparison was treating one repo as multiple distinct roots when spelled differently: VS Code sends lowercase drive letters (c:\…), spawn cwd has uppercase (C:\…), Git-for-Windows surfaces 8.3 short names. Raw string comparison caused false ambiguity rejections and unnecessary store re-preparation on every client connect. Touches invariant(s): con_2ce3f2a547 (Synthesis must use an explicitly selected coding-assistant subscription CLI or the deterministic local fallback; never call a pay-per-token API); con_e04226bd05 (The MCP server must stay client-agnostic: all assistants point to the same .hunch/ graph; no Claude-only behavior in the server).
decision: Introduced `canonicalRootPath(root: string)` that calls `realpathSync.native()` to resolve every root to its on-disk canonical spelling before any comparison or dedup. Applied everywhere roots are compared or deduplicated.
consequences: One logical repo never splits into multiple pseudo-roots due to case/spelling variance
Eliminates spurious store re-prepare on client reconnects with different path spellings
Removes entire class of Windows path-identity bugs while staying case-sensitive on POSIX
alternatives_rejected: Case-insensitive string comparison (doesn't handle 8.3 names; fragile on case-sensitive filesystems)
Scatter dedup logic throughout; accept multiple spellings as an operational hazard
Document the limitation and ask users to always use identical path spellings (poor UX)
